newsitem.title: USA: Crews work to control two U.S. Gulf well blowouts.
newsitem.headline: Crews work to control two U.S. Gulf well blowouts.

text.p: Crews were working on Thursday to shut in two separate natural gas well blowouts along the U.S. Gulf Coast, officials said.

Crews since Nov. 26 have been working to control a Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co well spewing 180 barrels per day of gas and condensate following a blowout on Nov. 26, a U.S. Coast Guard spokesman said.

The wet-gas well, located at Myette Point just off the Atchafalaya River in Louisiana, was killed Thursday when drilling mud was forced down the wellbore to stop the flow of gas and condensate, a company spokesman said.

In a separate incident, well firefighters from Boots & Coots were working to cap a dry-gas blowout at an Amoco Corp well in Eugene Island 224 about 60 miles off the coast of Louisiana, a Coast Guard spokesman said.
Workers were evacuated from the Amoco platform after the blowout of an exploitation well on December 3. There was no fire or injuries, an Amoco spokesman said.
"It's not a large blowout at all," the spokesman said.
